lens: SPEED-TO-CASH & PROBABILITY: the chance that the owner has actually received at least CAD 5,000 net by about Nov 30 2026 (roughly 9 weeks from today, 2026-09-23), and then averages CAD 5,000/month. I weighted four things: prepayment and deposit mechanics, sales-cycle length, late-September seasonality, and hard prerequisites (vehicle, ID-verified platform approval, reviews). Every fact comes from the bundle or corpus with a URL. Almost all market facts are search snippets the verifiers could not re-open. The only primary-verified facts are the federal statutes (ETA, CPP Act, EI Act and Regulations, CASL).

ranking.candidate: BUNDLE: Seasonal exterior home-services stack in one neighbourhood cluster (fall gutter/leaf cleanup Oct-Nov, paid per job; holiday-light installs, paid at install; seasonal snow contracts sold Oct-Nov and billed in instalments Dec-Mar). Conditional on the owner having a ladder-capable vehicle, fitness and comfort at heights
ranking.reason: Best timing fit of anything in the files. Three things are live right now. The gutter peak is 'late fall (after leaves drop, before snow)'. The GTA lights booking 'sweet spot is late September through the first week of October', though October callers 'can often be accommodated'. Snow contracts are sold before the season. Tickets are 5-20x a cleaning hour: gutters $150-$350 per job, lights $400-$1,500 per home, snow $400-$1,500 per season in the GTA. ESTIMATE of cash by Nov 30: 12 gutter jobs x $245 contribution = $2,940, plus 5 light installs x $570 = $2,850, gives $5,790 before any snow money. One door-knock can pitch all three services (my judgement, not sourced). Incumbents do bundle lights with exterior services (Shack Shine, Calgary landscapers). Two limits. First, winter falls short: snow alone needs about 46 contracts at $600 (65 at $400) to reach $5k/month in season, which is beyond evidenced solo capacity. Second, January brings an unpaid lights takedown. Everything is gated on vehicle, ladder and insurance, all unknown for this owner. All prices are unverified snippets.

ranking.candidate: cand_cleaning (residential deep and move-out cleaning via TaskRabbit/Jiffy plus direct Kijiji, FB and Korean-community leads)

Jiffy pays the Friday after the job week. No seasonal cliff was found, but seasonality is marked NOT FOUND rather than proven flat. ESTIMATE: $5,000 cumulative by Nov 30 at $45/hr = 111 billable hours over about 8 weeks, about 14 h/week. That is plausible even from zero reviews. Negatives: platform approval time is not found, and the price inputs conflict ($15-$30, $35-$65 and $85-$125/hr). Sustaining $5k/month needs 26-41 billable h/wk, or 35-45+ h/wk once unpaid time is counted. The best choice as the floor and the winter line.

Paid at completion. The peak falls inside the window (late Oct-Nov). 22 jobs x $265 ≈ $5,830 gross/month (dossier arithmetic confirmed). Early October is before the peak, so first cash comes around week 2 and volume later. It hard-requires a vehicle for a 24-28 ft ladder. Toronto pressure washing likely needs a Building Renovator licence and exam. The Dec-Mar cliff has no winter line.

The only candidate with a structural prepayment mechanism in Oct-Nov. GTA precedent: a company offered a prepay discount and one customer paid $1,200 upfront for 2025-26. ESTIMATE: about 9-10 contracts at $550-$600 = $5k collected. Three problems. Ontario door-to-door direct agreements carry a 10-day cooling-off right with refund within 15 days (search summary). Quebec's OPC advises consumers against any deposit before service starts. The same GTA prepay precedent ended in 'feel cheated' news coverage, which damages trust for newcomers. Prepaid money is an unearned liability until snow falls. Insurance timing, snowfall and solo capacity are unknown. Vancouver is not evidenced.

High ticket, paid at install from late Oct. ESTIMATE: 9-12 homes = $5k contribution (5,000/570 = 8.8; 5,000/445 with a helper = 11.2). But the booking window is closing now, most GTA firms are full by mid-November, and deposit norms were not found. The owner would enter with no reviews against franchises. Revenue is zero Feb-Sep, and the source prices conflict 2-3x. Useful only as a layer on the exterior stack.

But TaskRabbit 'doesn't guarantee all applications will be processed' because of saturation, and approval time is not found. The new-Tasker ramp is $1,000-1,500/month per blogs. October is likely off-peak for moves (unverified). Works best inside the same TaskRabbit account as cleaning, adding to the floor.

The dossier's typical first cash is day 37-75. Payout holds are 5 days for Upwork fixed-price, about 10 days for hourly, and 14 days for new Fiverr sellers. Upwork's reported active clients are -4% YoY (snippet). Both ends fall outside the window.

Toronto median net is $5.97/hr across all road time. $5k would need about 193 h/week (ESTIMATE). Onboarding time is not found. Rideshare must register for GST/HST from the first dollar (ETA s.240(1.1), verified). Useful at most as a few hundred dollars of bridge cash.

Follower and watch-hour gates block payouts: YPP needs 1k subs plus 4k hours, and TikTok needs 10k followers. Tool affiliate commission is about 3%. The dossier's own realistic 60-day outcome is CAD 0-500/month.
The TrustMRR year-0 median is $148 MRR. Median time to $1K MRR is 8 months even among survivors. Hitting the target needs about 418 new C$9 subscribers every month from launch (ESTIMATE).

recommended_primary: A seasonal exterior home-services stack sold street by street in one neighbourhood cluster: fall gutter/eavestrough and leaf cleanup now (paid per job), holiday-light installs (customer-owned-lights option to limit capital; paid at install; take a deposit only through the owner's own account), and seasonal snow-clearing contracts sold in October-November and billed in 2-3 instalments over Dec-Mar, not one lump prepayment. Hard gate to decide by about Sep 30: the owner must have a vehicle that can carry a 24-28 ft ladder, be physically fit and comfortable at heights, and be able to bind liability insurance in October. If any gate fails, drop gutters and lights, make cleaning the primary, and keep only walkable-cluster shovel/snowblower contracts as the add-on. City notes: GTA and Ottawa fit best. In Ottawa, a vehicle-mounted plow needs a licence and $2M insurance, and lights 'fill up by October'. Calgary snow sells monthly ($129-$300/month). Metro Vancouver: snow is not evidenced, so drop it. Montreal: French is required, and the OPC gives a 10-day cancellation right and advises consumers against deposits. Pricing is not found for Montreal.
recommended_parallel: A cleaning floor starting in week 1, whatever the gate outcome: residential deep and move-out cleans through TaskRabbit ($25 fee, reported) and Jiffy (paid the Friday after the job week), plus direct Kijiji/Facebook/Korean-community leads that the owner posts, with light TaskRabbit assembly/TV-mount tasks on the same account. It fills the January-March gap the exterior stack leaves. ESTIMATE of a winter blend: 25 snow contracts x $500 = $12,500 / 5 months = $2,500/month, plus cleaning $2,500/month = 56 billable h/month at $45 (about 13 h/week), for about $5,000/month. Before either line starts, file the EI claim no later than Saturday Oct 10 2026, so the benefit period begins Oct 4 inside the Pilot 24 window (possible waiting-week waiver; separation pay not counted as earnings). Then choose explicitly. Path A: a declared side activity kept 'minor in extent', where EI is cut by 50% of earnings up to 90% of weekly insurable earnings. Path B: the full business, where EI is $0 for every week it runs. ESTIMATE: at the $729/week maximum, EI is worth about $3,159/month (729 x 52 / 12). A full-time business has to beat that before it adds anything in Oct-Nov.

key_facts_relied_on.fact: GTA holiday-light booking: 'the sweet spot is late September through the first week of October'; 'Most reputable GTA companies are fully booked by mid-November'; 'New clients who reach out in October can often be accommodated' (search summary, corpus S065; verifier: unverifiable, vendor blog).
GTA light installation pricing: single-storey $400-$800, two-storey $700-$1,500, large $1,500-$3,000+ (snippet, unverifiable). Deposit and payment-timing norms: not found.
Gutter cleaning should be done 'in late fall (after leaves drop, before snow)'. Calgary: bungalow $150-$225, 2-storey $225-$275 (snippet).
Toronto standard residential gutter cleaning $150-$350 (2026 guide, snippet, unverifiable).
Toronto: most homeowners pay $500-$1,500 per season for flat-rate snow removal. Other GTA guides show $200-$600 and $400-$950; per-visit $50-$150 (snippets).

GTA precedent for prepaid snow contracts: a company offered a discount for paying in advance for 2025-26, one customer paid $1,200, and service stopped after one visit. Customers 'feel cheated' (CP24, Jan 16 2026, via corpus S045 summary).

Ontario Consumer Protection Act: direct agreements made at the consumer's home (door-to-door, including snow removal) can be cancelled within 10 days of receiving the signed copy, with a refund within 15 days (search summary, corpus S037; not verified on ontario.ca).

Quebec OPC: paying the whole snow contract before service starts is a risk borne by the consumer, and it is 'recommended not to give any deposit' before service begins. Spread payments, e.g. two instalments. 10 days to cancel if solicited at home (corpus S038 summary).

Snow insurance: general liability 'typically starts at around $450 per year for a $2 million coverage limit' (snippet). One broker page says insurers restrict snow policies by late autumn (verifier: single broker source, unverified).
Toronto cleaning: $35-$65/hr per cleaner, reputable firms $45-$55 (snippet). The sources conflict with $85-$125/hr (HomeStars) and $15-$30 for independents.

TaskRabbit Canada: one-time non-refundable $25 Tasker registration fee, and paying it does not guarantee acceptance (snippet). NerdWallet says applications may not be processed, to avoid oversaturation.
Jiffy pays pros on the Friday after the week the job was done; commission reportedly 12-18% (up to 25-30% per app reviews). Search summary.

EI Regulations s.30(1)-(3): a claimant operating a business is considered to have worked a full working week (no EI) unless the business is 'to such a minor extent' that it would not normally be relied on as a principal livelihood. The factors include time, capital, success, continuity and willingness to take other work. Primary statute, verified.

EI Act s.19(2): benefit reduced by 50% of earnings up to 90% of weekly insurable earnings and 100% above. s.14(1): the rate is 55%. The 2026 maximum is about $729/week (secondary source plus formula check: 68,900 / 52 x 0.55 = 728.75).

EI Pilot Project No. 24 (Regs ss.77.996-77.999): waiting period may be waived, and separation earnings are not counted, for benefit periods beginning Mar 30 2025 - Oct 10 2026. Benefit period begins the Sunday of the week of the claim (EI Act s.10(1)). So a claim by Sat Oct 10 2026 starts Oct 4. Extension beyond Oct 10: not found.

GST/HST small supplier: $30,000 over four calendar quarters, with status lasting through the quarter plus the first following month (ETA s.148(1)). Rideshare/taxi must register from the first dollar (s.240(1.1)). Ontario HST is 13%. Primary statute.
Self-employed CPP: 9.9% base + 2.0% first additional (Schedules 1-2), $3,500 basic exemption (s.20(2)). ESTIMATE about $560/month at $60k/yr net.

CASL: consent is required for commercial electronic messages (email, SMS, IM). Implied consent covers conspicuously published business addresses relevant to the recipient's role, and inquiries (6 months). The sender bears the onus. Penalty up to $1M for an individual. Live two-way voice calls are excluded. Door-to-door and printed flyers are not electronic messages.
Toronto median ride-hail net was $5.97/hr across all time on the road (Jan-Apr 2024, City of Toronto analysis via Globe snippet).

Upwork: fixed-price funds released 5 days after approval, hourly pay about 10 days after the billing week. Fiverr new-seller earnings clear after 14 days. Guides put the first job at 2-8 weeks (snippets).

Google Business Profile verification review can take up to 5 business days, and postcards up to 14 days (secondary playbook dated 2026-07-06). Maps visibility should not be counted on for October income.

Consumer Interac e-Transfer limits are typically $2,000-3,000 per transaction and set per bank (secondary). An Oakville contractor had a $1,972 balance delayed by an e-transfer limit. Large snow or lights tickets may need split payments or card links.
The owner's scraper returned 0 prices for all 54 queries on every snapshot from 2026-08-05 to 2026-09-23 (verified locally by the resell verifier).

notes:
WHY THIS RANKING (lens: cash actually received by Nov 30, then sustained):
(1) It is late September. The only candidates whose demand peaks inside Oct-Nov and pay per ticket at completion or install are fall exterior work and holiday lights. Snow is the only one with a sales window now and money collected before service. Every digital or platform option has a gate (reviews, follower thresholds, payout holds, approval queues) that pushes typical first cash past day 30. The dossiers' own estimates are day 37-75 on freelance platforms, CAD 0-500 at day 60 for content, and a $148 year-0 median MRR for SaaS.
(2) Cash by Nov 30 at modest volumes. ESTIMATE, exterior stack: 12 gutter jobs x $245 + 5 light installs x $570 = $2,940 + $2,850 = $5,790. ESTIMATE, cleaning only: 5,000 / 45 = 111 billable h over about 8 weeks, about 14 h/week.
(3) Sustaining $5k/month is where every seasonal line fails on its own. Gutters: Dec-Mar cliff. Lights: zero Feb-Sep, and the January takedown is unpaid. Snow: 46+ contracts at $600 is beyond evidenced solo capacity. So cleaning is paired in as the winter carrier.

TREAT PREPAYMENT AS CASH, NOT INCOME. Snow prepayments are real cash in hand but also an unearned liability. Ontario direct agreements carry a 10-day cooling-off right with a 15-day refund (search summary). The CP24 Jan-2026 'Snow Pros' story shows GTA homeowners have been burned by prepay, so a newcomer should offer instalments (deposit plus a mid-season payment) and a written contract with no-snow-onto-road and low-snow terms. ESTIMATE: 10 contracts x $600 = $6,000 collected, but only about $1,200/month of it is earned over a 5-month season.

EI IS THE BIGGEST HIDDEN VARIABLE for the 30-day need, and the dossiers largely missed it. If the owner qualifies, EI at the maximum is worth about $3,159/month (ESTIMATE 729 x 52 / 12). A full-scale business makes each operating week pay $0 EI (Regs s.30). Filing by Oct 10 keeps the Pilot 24 benefits available. Whether to run the business beyond 'minor in extent' in October should be decided with Service Canada, not assumed. Eligibility (insurable hours, reason for job loss, severance) is unknown.

GATING UNKNOWNS that change the answer. Vehicle, fitness, heights comfort and English level decide between the exterior stack and cleaning as primary. Savings decide whether insurance, a ladder or snowblower and a GST-free runway are affordable; snowblower and Canadian ladder prices were not found. Every market price here is an unverified search snippet (all non-GitHub domains were blocked), so the AI should build quote calculators with editable price inputs, not hard-coded 'facts'.

WHAT THE AI SHOULD BUILD FIRST (supports speed). A one-page bilingual EN/KO site, deployed to Cloudflare Pages because Vercel Hobby is reported non-commercial. Door-hanger and flyer PDFs combining fall, lights and snow offers. A snow contract with a cooling-off notice, instalment schedule and low-snow clause (for a lawyer to review). A cleaning/TaskRabbit profile and a checklist pack. A route and CRM sheet. An EI weekly-earnings declaration tracker. A GST $30k and CPP set-aside tracker. Flyers and door-knocking avoid CASL. Any email or SMS follow-up must carry CASL identification and an unsubscribe.

CITY DIFFERENCES (from the files only). GTA: evidence strongest. Ottawa: vehicle-plow licence, $2M insurance, 30+ snow events, lights 'fill up by October'. Calgary: snow billed monthly $129-$300; a gutter competitor advertises from $75. Metro Vancouver: no snow evidence; lights $8-$12/ft; gutters $100-$300; BC gig floor $21.89 per engaged hour. Montreal: French selling, QPP/QST, OPC anti-deposit guidance; prices not found.

lens: DOWNGRADE & ROBUSTNESS: how much capital is at risk; legal and regulatory exposure (CASL, licensing, insurance, liability, EI, GST/HST); physical and safety risk; and how much each option depends on owner attributes that are UNKNOWN (vehicle, English fluency, trade skills, savings). Options that still work with little capital and average skills score higher, and car dependence is penalized. I read all 17 bundle files. Verifier corrections override dossier claims. Only the federal statute facts (Justice Canada XML on GitHub) and Cloudflare docs were confirmed from primary text. Everything else is at search-snippet level, and I treat it that way below.

ranking.candidate: cleaning (residential deep clean / move-in-move-out at flat rates, recurring clients; TaskRabbit/Jiffy for first reviews, then direct booking)
ranking.reason: The most robust option that still has a plausible path to $5k. Capital is small: the only sourced cost is the $25 TaskRabbit fee, and supplies were not found. No licence was found, though that is unverified. It needs no vehicle, though one helps (dossier). The skill involved is average and trainable, not a trade. It works in every metro and is not tied to the weather; seasonality was not found. Unlike gutters, lights and snow, there is no work at height. Downsides: the owner does physical labour and carries the risk of damage or theft claims. Insurance cost is unverified; one snippet says 'can start at $500 for self-employed cleaners', with unclear attribution. The price inputs conflict ($15–30, $35–65 and $85–125/hr). The verifier puts probability_5k at 2.5, which is still the highest of the low-capital, low-skill options.

ranking.candidate: tutoring (direct-pay K-12 curriculum / Korean language, online or at the library)
ranking.reason: Low capital: about $72 for a VSC plus existing devices. No licence is needed in Ontario (OCT help snippet). Physical risk is near zero. K-12 curriculum tutoring is HST-exempt (CRA Memo 20-6 snippet), and no vehicle is needed if it is done online or at a library. But it depends entirely on an UNKNOWN subject skill and English level. There is liability exposure with minors, and it is unclear whether a self-employed person can obtain a VSC. The verifier's probability is 1.5. This is a strong conditional secondary line, not a primary one.

ranking.candidate: labour (TaskRabbit furniture assembly / TV mounting only; no truck categories)
ranking.reason: Uses the same $25 TaskRabbit account as cleaning, and assembly and mounting need tools but no vehicle. Downsides: property-damage liability (dropped TVs, walls), and the regulated-trade boundary is unverified, since in-wall power requests are likely regulated electrical work. The IKEA payout depends on speed ($20/hr for a beginner vs $50/hr for a fast worker, per a blog snippet). TaskRabbit may not process applications in saturated cities (NerdWallet snippet). Works best bundled with cleaning to fill the schedule, not on its own.

Very safe on capital and physical risk, and the AI does most of the delivery. But revenue depends completely on the owner's UNKNOWN business English and sales ability. CASL puts the burden of proving consent on the sender (s.13), the maximum penalty for an individual is $1M (s.20(4)), and cold email to consumers is prohibited. The verifier found the dossier's own 60-day scenario averages about $3k/month, not $5k. Only a small legal risk remains if it is sold in person or through inbound inquiries. Keep it as upside only if the owner has English and SMB contacts.

Near-zero capital and no physical or licence risk. But it depends heavily on English and on proven skills, both UNKNOWN. Cash arrives slowly: the typical case is day 37–75, and Fiverr holds funds for 14 days. Upwork active clients fell 4% (snippet). If the owner cannot pay rent in month 1, being slow is itself the downside.

ranking.candidate: korean (KO/EN bilingual websites for Korean-owned SMBs; translation)
ranking.reason: Low capital, but the community pulls toward paid immigration paperwork help, and that is legally closed without CICC or law-society authorization (canada.ca snippet: anyone compensated 'in any way' must be authorized). Uncertified IRCC translation likely loses money once the affidavit/notary cost is included (verifier ESTIMATE: $45 price − $75 notarization proxy = −$30 per document). It needs both native Korean and professional English. The website line has no evidence of price or demand.

Little capital (US$5 CWS fee) and no physical or licence risk, but it depends on UNKNOWN savings to fund a runway. The year-0 median is $148/month MRR (TrustMRR, n=5,079), and the median time to $1K MRR is 8 months. For someone who needs income within 30 days, the realistic downside is no income, even though the cash at risk is small.

Rideshare must register for GST/HST from the first dollar (ETA s.240(1.1), verified in the statute). Ride-hail needs a car, insurance gaps are unverified, and the Toronto median net was $5.97/hr across all road time (snippet, Jan–Apr 2024). There is road and fatigue risk. Bike delivery lowers the capital needed, but its earnings are unknown. Onboarding and payout timing were not found. It can serve as a small cash bridge but offers no path to $5k.

Carries slip-and-fall and property-damage liability. Prepayments are a liability owed back through March if the operator is injured. One broker page says insurers restrict cover by late autumn (unverified). Throwing snow onto the road draws HTA and bylaw fines, and Ottawa requires a plow licence plus $2M insurance for vehicle plows. The owner would need a snowblower (price not found) and ideally a vehicle. Weather cuts both ways, and Metro Vancouver snowfall data was not found. Almost nothing is earned in Oct–Nov.

Low cash at risk, but reaching income depends on having savings runway. The platform gates (YPP, TikTok 10k followers) and the 3% tool commission require large volumes. The existing repo's Amazon scraper uses a spoofed User-Agent, which may conflict with the Associates agreement (unverified), and it shows prices more than 5 months stale. There is no realistic path to 30-day income.

A vehicle that can carry a 24–28 ft ladder is mandatory, and whether the owner has one is UNKNOWN. Ladder falls are the dominant risk. Pressure washing in Toronto appears to require the Building Renovator licence with an exam (snippet). Working at Heights applicability is ambiguous. The insurance quote is a window-cleaning quote, not a gutter quote. The verifier's low_risk score is 2.

This option has the most capital at risk: an estimated $4k–$19k to approach $5k/month, and that money comes from the survival fund of someone who just lost a job. There is dead-inventory and pallet-dud risk. DeWalt ungating failed for 5 months in one report, and Amazon account suspensions can freeze payouts. Returns pallets can contain personal data. A vehicle and storage are needed for anything bulky.

Worst on downside. It involves ladder and roof work in Nov–Jan ice. A vehicle and ladders are mandatory. The lease model means buying lights upfront before customers pay. The January takedown is prepaid, so it is unpaid labour in bad weather. The GTA booking window is 'September through early October' and firms are 'fully booked by mid-November' (settoshine snippet), so a zero-review entrant is late. Canadian insurance cost and exclusions were not found.

recommended_primary: A residential cleaning service in the GTA focused on flat-rate deep cleans and move-in/move-out cleans, plus recurring biweekly clients. Launch through TaskRabbit (and Jiffy if accepted) to get first reviews, and in parallel run an AI-built bilingual EN/KO direct-booking site with an instant quote calculator. It works without a car: take transit-reachable jobs first and pack a portable supply kit. The owner must get a liability-insurance quote before taking any direct (off-platform) client; the cost is unverified. Why this wins under a downside lens: little capital at stake, no licence found, no work at heights, not seasonal or weather-dependent, and doable with average skills and functional English. It also carries over to every metro. Vancouver: BC STR rules cut entire-home listings 22%, so skip STR turnover. Calgary/Ottawa: rates not found, check locally. Montreal: QPP and QST instead of CPP/HST, Quebec privacy law applies, and French is likely needed (unverified). Honest expectation from the verifier: probability 2.5/10 of averaging $5k net in the first 60 days. A $5k run-rate by month 2–3 is plausible only for a fit owner working about 32–43 h/week. ESTIMATE: 6,250/45 = 138.9 billable h/month = 32.1 h/week; ÷0.75 for unbillable time = 42.8 h/week. Marketing design keeps CASL exposure near zero: flyers and door-to-door (not commercial electronic messages), replies to inbound inquiries (SOR/2013-221 s.3(b)), requested quotes (CASL s.6(6)(a)), and no cold email or SMS to consumers. Host the site on Cloudflare Pages, not Vercel Hobby (non-commercial only).
recommended_parallel: INCOME FLOOR = EI, handled explicitly. (1) File the initial EI claim right after the last day of work, and no later than Saturday October 10, 2026. That puts the benefit period start (Sunday October 4) inside Pilot Project No. 24 (EI Regs ss.77.996–77.999): a possible waiting-week waiver (discretionary), separation money not counted as earnings, and +20 weeks for long-tenured workers. No extension beyond October 10 was found. Maximum benefit is about $729/week (secondary source plus the statute formula). ESTIMATE: 729 × 52 / 12 ≈ $3,159/month at most; the owner's actual rate is unknown. (2) Stage the business. Under EI Regs s.30(1), any week the business is more than 'minor in extent' counts as a full working week, which pays $0 EI. So in October, run cleaning at small declared volume and report net earnings. EI Act s.19(2): benefits are reduced by 50% of earnings up to 90% of weekly insurable earnings. ESTIMATE: $400 net → EI $529 + $400 = $929 that week. Go full-time and stop claiming only once weekly business net reliably exceeds the EI rate. Confirm the minor-extent treatment with Service Canada first; undeclared earnings are clawed back (s.19(3)). (3) BACKUP on the same TaskRabbit account ($25): furniture assembly and TV mounting (no in-wall electrical) to fill gaps in the schedule. (4) CONDITIONAL add-ons, only if the owner confirms the attribute: direct-pay K-12 or Korean tutoring (needs subject skill; no licence), and KO/EN websites for Korean SMBs sold in person (needs business English or Korean networks; never paid immigration paperwork).

key_facts_relied_on.fact: CASL implied consent by conspicuous publication applies only if the address was conspicuously published with no 'no unsolicited CEMs' statement and the message is relevant to the recipient's business role. The sender bears the onus of proof (s.13). The maximum penalty is $1,000,000 for an individual (s.20(4)). Live two-way voice calls are excluded from s.6 (s.6(8)(a)). Consent is not needed for the first commercial electronic message after a referral, if the message names the referrer and says it is sent because of the referral (SOR/2013-221 s.4(1)).

EI Regs s.30(1): a claimant running a business on their own account is considered to have worked a full working week, unless the business is 'minor in extent' (s.30(2)), judged on time, capital, success, continuity and willingness to take other work (s.30(3)).

EI Pilot Project No. 24: the waiting-period waiver (discretionary, 'may') and the exclusion of separation money apply to benefit periods beginning by October 10, 2026. A claim made in the week of Sunday October 4, 2026 starts the benefit period on October 4 (EI Act s.10(1)). No extension was found.
